title: IBM, RIKEN, and NVIDIA Achieve 79x Accuracy Gain in Quantum-Classical Simulations of Iron-Sulfur Clusters - Quantum Computing Report
gist: IBM Quantum, RIKEN and NVIDIA improved Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) energy accuracy 79-fold on an iron-sulfur [4Fe-4S] cluster by seeding it with broken-symmetry UHF reference states, running on ibm_kingston plus RIKEN's NVIDIA GB200-powered ROQUO; the extrapolated result matched classical DMRG within 0.33 mHa. The work positions reference-state preparation as a primary SQD accuracy lever in quantum-centric supercomputing.

insights.claim: IBM Quantum, RIKEN and NVIDIA achieved a 79-fold energy-accuracy improvement in quantum-classical simulation of iron-sulfur clusters by initializing Sample-Based Quantum Diagonalization (SQD) with broken-symmetry unrestricted Hartree-Fock (BS-UHF) reference states.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid quantum-HPC chemistry is producing measurable accuracy gains; a proof point for IBM's quantum-centric supercomputing pitch.
insights.locator: Researchers from IBM Quantum, RIKEN, and NVIDIA

insights.claim: Running on IBM's ibm_kingston processor and RIKEN's ROQUO supercomputer, broken-symmetry SQD brought the 72-qubit [Fe4S4(SCH3)4]2− active-space ground-state energy within 4.3 millihartree of high-precision classical DMRG benchmarks, and its d→∞ extrapolation matched extrapolated DMRG within 0.33 mHa.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum methods are reaching parity with, not beating, classical DMRG — accuracy validation, not quantum advantage.
insights.locator: Executed on the ibm_kingston quantum processor

insights.claim: The Fe-S SQD experiment ran a 1-layer LUCJ circuit with 3,944 CZ gates and two-qubit depth 276 on 88 active qubits of ibm_kingston, using 5 million hardware shots (~25 minutes of QPU time).
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Useful chemistry workloads now run deep circuits on ~88-qubit devices in under half an hour of QPU time.

themes.theme: Reference state as key accuracy lever

insights.claim: Previous SQD studies seeded with restricted Hartree-Fock (RHF) determinants stalled more than 500 millihartree above exact ground-state energies for iron-sulfur clusters even at large subspace dimensions, because antiferromagnetically coupled iron centers create dense multireference correlations.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Naive SQD setups fail on strongly correlated chemistry — algorithmic choices determine whether quantum chemistry is useful.
insights.locator: Iron-sulfur cubane clusters play central roles

insights.claim: Spin-polarized, fragment-localized Noodleman BS-UHF initial guesses steer quantum sampling toward chemically relevant magnetic configurations, lowering the starting mean-field energy by ~534 mHa versus closed-shell RHF and yielding SQD energies 512–517 mHa deeper than RHF-seeded SQD.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Classical pre-processing know-how is a moat in quantum chemistry software; watch IBM's Qiskit/SQD ecosystem.
insights.locator: By extending the open-source qcsc-prefect workflow

insights.claim: The IBM–RIKEN–NVIDIA study identifies reference-state preparation as a primary driver of SQD accuracy alongside subspace size and GPU-accelerated Davidson diagonalization.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Framework for judging hybrid chemistry claims: check reference state, subspace dimension, and classical compute budget.
insights.quote: highlights reference-state preparation as a primary driver of SQD accuracy

insights.claim: SQD configuration recovery for the Fe-S cluster scaled to 36 nodes (144 NVIDIA GB200 GPUs) of RIKEN's ROQUO, with checkpoints portable across JCAHPC's Miyabi-G GPU cluster and RIKEN's CPU-based Fugaku supercomputer via the open-source qcsc-prefect workflow.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum chemistry pipelines consume large GPU allocations — quantum progress is incremental demand for NVIDIA accelerators.
insights.locator: After validating the method on a 40-qubit

insights.claim: Before scaling to the [4Fe-4S] cluster, the researchers validated broken-symmetry SQD on a 40-qubit [2Fe-2S] dimer using IBM's ibm_fez processor.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Staged validation suggests a repeatable methodology that may extend to larger metalloenzyme systems.
insights.locator: After validating the method on a 40-qubit

insights.claim: Japan's New Energy and Industrial Technology Development Organization (NEDO) funded the IBM–RIKEN–NVIDIA iron-sulfur SQD study under its quantum-supercomputer hybrid platform initiative.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Japanese government funding is anchoring quantum-HPC integration, supporting IBM and NVIDIA's footprint in Japan.
